comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses increased for fiscal year 2024 due to growth in employees and compensation increases, while the prior year included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both discuss drivers of operating expenses in fiscal year 2024, but focus on different components. AVGO highlights $1,533 million in restructuring charges (employee termination) as a key operating expense item. In contrast, NVDA highlights that operating expenses increased due to growth in employees and compensation increases, noting the prior year included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge. While both reference significant one-time or restructuring-like costs affecting the P&L, AVGO's 2024 charges are primarily merger-related severance, whereas NVDA's comparable context emphasizes compensation growth and excludes its prior-year acquisition termination.
